# India's New Tax & Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026: Decoding the Impact on Investment & Digital Payments

The Indian regulatory landscape, as we all know, is a dynamic one. Just when you think you've got a handle on things, a new amendment comes along, making us professionals rethink our strategies. This time, it's the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, which received Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and was published in the Official Gazette on the very same day. Yeh toh chalta hi rehta hai, right? But what does this latest legislative move mean for businesses, investors, and even our everyday digital transactions? Let's dive deep.

This Act isn't just a minor tweak; it's a comprehensive piece of legislation aiming to further streamline the tax framework, attract foreign capital, and boost domestic manufacturing and digital adoption. It amends several crucial Acts, including the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. Notably, it also formally repeals the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, which was promulgated on June 5, 2026, while safeguarding actions already taken under it. Unless specifically provided otherwise for a particular section, the Act is generally deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2026.

## Rationalizing Business Connection for Foreign Funds: A Game-Changer for Fund Managers

One of the most significant changes, particularly for the financial services sector and foreign investors, is the rationalization of conditions for eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. The government has further simplified the "safe harbour" provisions, making India a more attractive destination for fund management activities.

                                                                                                        | The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**: A Deep Dive for Professionals

Greetings, fellow professionals! The recent enactment of the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, receiving Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and swiftly published in the Official Gazette, marks another pivotal moment in India's continuously evolving legal and economic landscape. As seasoned practitioners, we understand that these legislative updates are not just academic exercises; they carry real-world implications, shaping business strategies and compliance requirements. This Act, in particular, seems to have a clear focus: enhancing India's attractiveness for foreign investment, bolstering domestic manufacturing, and refining our digital payment infrastructure. So, chalo, let's unpack this for a clearer picture.

This comprehensive Act modifies several key legislations, notably the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. For context, remember that the Income-tax Act, 2025, itself replaced the erstwhile Income-tax Act, 1961. The new Act also formally replaces the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, which was promulgated on June 5, 2026, ensuring that any actions taken under the Ordinance remain valid. While specific provisions might have distinct effective dates, the Act is generally deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2026.

Let's dissect some of the most impactful amendments.

## Driving Fund Management to India: Rationalized Safe Harbour Norms

One of the standout features of this Act is the significant rationalization of conditions concerning eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This move is a clear signal of the government's intent to encourage the relocation of fund management activities to India by making the "safe harbour" provisions more practical and less cumbersome.

Greetings, fellow professionals! The recent enactment of the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, receiving Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and swiftly published in the Official Gazette, marks another pivotal moment in India's continuously evolving legal and economic landscape. As seasoned practitioners, we understand that these legislative updates are not just academic exercises; they carry real-world implications, shaping business strategies and compliance requirements. This Act, in particular, seems to have a clear focus: enhancing India's attractiveness for foreign investment, bolstering domestic manufacturing, and refining our digital payment infrastructure. So, chalo, let's unpack this for a clearer picture.

This comprehensive Act modifies several key legislations, notably the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. For context, remember that the Income-tax Act, 2025, itself replaced the erstwhile Income-tax Act, 1961. The new Act also formally replaces the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, which was promulgated on June 5, 2026, ensuring that any actions taken under the Ordinance remain valid. While specific provisions might have distinct effective dates, the Act is generally deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2026.

Let's dissect some of the most impactful amendments.

## Driving Fund Management to India: Rationalized Safe Harbour Norms

One of the standout features of this Act is the significant rationalization of conditions concerning eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This move is a clear signal of the government's intent to encourage the relocation of fund management activities to India by making the "safe harbour" provisions more practical and less cumbersome.

Greetings, fellow professionals! The recent enactment of the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, receiving Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and swiftly published in the Official Gazette, marks another pivotal moment in India's continuously evolving legal and economic landscape. As seasoned practitioners, we understand that these legislative updates are not just academic exercises; they carry real-world implications, shaping business strategies and compliance requirements. This Act, in particular, seems to have a clear focus: enhancing India's attractiveness for foreign investment, bolstering domestic manufacturing, and refining our digital payment infrastructure. This comprehensive Act modifies several key legislations, notably the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. ## Driving Fund Management to India: Rationalized Safe Harbour Norms

One of the standout features of this Act is the significant rationalization of conditions concerning eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This move is a clear signal of the government's intent to encourage the relocation of fund management activities to India by making the "safe harbour" provisions more practical and less cumbersome.

                                                              The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, which received Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and was published in the Official Gazette on the same date, brings forth significant changes aimed at bolstering India's economic framework. This Act isn't merely a set of isolated amendments; it reflects a strategic legislative approach to attract foreign investment, promote domestic electronics manufacturing, and provide much-needed clarity in digital payment regulations. As professionals navigating India's dynamic regulatory environment, understanding these shifts is paramount for effective advisory and compliance.

This comprehensive piece of legislation amends several critical Acts, including the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. It's worth noting that the Income-tax Act, 2025, itself is a relatively new law, having replaced the earlier Income-tax Act, 1961. Furthermore, the Act officially repeals the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, which was promulgated on June 5, 2026, while explicitly safeguarding actions already taken under it. Unless otherwise specified for a particular provision, the Act is generally deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2026.

Let's delve into some of the most impactful amendments.

## Driving Fund Management to India: Rationalized Safe Harbour Norms

One of the standout features of this Act is the significant rationalization of conditions concerning eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This move is a clear signal of the government's intent to encourage the relocation of fund management activities to India by making the "safe harbour" provisions more practical and less cumbersome.

                                                                                        | The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**: A Deep Dive for Professionals

Greetings, fellow professionals! The recent enactment of the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, receiving Presidential Assent on August 17, 2026, and swiftly published in the Official Gazette, marks another pivotal moment in India's continuously evolving legal and economic landscape. As seasoned practitioners, we understand that these legislative updates are not just academic exercises; they carry real-world implications, shaping business strategies and compliance requirements. This Act, in particular, seems to have a clear focus: enhancing India's attractiveness for foreign investment, bolstering domestic manufacturing, and refining our digital payment infrastructure. So, chalo, let's unpack this for a clearer picture.

This comprehensive Act modifies several key legislations, notably the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, the **Income-tax Act, 2025**, and the **Finance Act, 2026**. For context, remember that the Income-tax Act, 2025, itself replaced the erstwhile Income-tax Act, 1961. The new Act also formally replaces the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, which was promulgated on June 5, 2026, ensuring that any actions taken under the Ordinance remain valid. While specific provisions might have distinct effective dates, the Act is generally deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2026.

Let's dissect some of the most impactful amendments.

## Driving Fund Management to India: Rationalized Safe Harbour Norms

One of the standout features of this Act is the significant rationalization of conditions concerning eligible investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. This move is a clear signal of the government's intent to encourage the relocation of fund management activities to India by making the "safe harbour" provisions more practical and less cumbersome.

The extension of income tax exemptions provides much-needed long-term policy certainty, which is critical for attracting substantial foreign direct investment and fostering an ecosystem for electronics production.
